q: Fortnow-Kummer (and others) proved results on the random-regular sequence in terms of Kolmogorov complexity. An infinite sequence X = x₁x₂… is computably random (Schnorr random) if:
opts: Every computable martingale fails to succeed on X (makes no unbounded profit betting on X)
X passes all computable statistical tests
exp: Schnorr randomness: X is Schnorr random iff no computable martingale succeeds (wins unboundedly) on X. This is strictly weaker than Martin-Löf randomness (which uses effective null sets / prefix complexity). The three main notions form a strict hierarchy: Schnorr ⊂ computable ⊂ Martin-Löf.
